title: How to use Claude 4.6 — the full cheat sheet
blurb: Model selector, every feature explained, and a goal→action→example map. The single best orientation doc for the Claude product surface.
body:
A complete orientation to the Claude 4.6 product surface.

Pick your model

  • Opus 4.6 — most capable: complex reasoning, advanced coding, large datasets/codebases.
  • Sonnet 4.6 — smart + fast: everyday tasks, general problem-solving, cost efficiency.
  • Haiku 4.5 — fastest/most compact: simple tasks, high-volume automation.

The feature toolbox

  • Artifacts — interactive, editable content (apps, docs, dashboards); real-time, supports HTML/React/Python.
  • Web Search — current info with citations.
  • Analysis Tool — runs JavaScript for data analysis & complex math.
  • File Upload — PDF/DOCX/CSV/images; document review, extraction.
  • Connectors — Slack, Drive, Notion, Figma & more via MCP.
  • Projects — organize chats/files under one long-running objective.
  • Research — multi-step online synthesis with citations.
  • Claude Code — agentic coding in terminal/Desktop/web (Pro/Max).
  • Cowork — agent working with local files & browser (Max, macOS).
  • Skills — reusable instruction sets that auto-trigger; brand guides, workflows.
  • Memory — remembers context across conversations; builds a summary of preferences.

Goal → example

Create artifacts ("build a budget tracker web app") · Trigger web search ("latest on Tesla stock?") · Use analysis ("analyze this sales data") · Start research ("research sustainable energy in Asia") · Use Skills ("create a skill that formats reports in my brand style") · Use Memory ("based on last week, update the plan").

SOURCE · Charlie Hills, "How to use Claude 4.6."
